spec_features.spec_quote: Reproducibility and low confounds over maximal elicitation
spec_features.evidence: Deterministic seeding (config.py:61 seed=20240601; harness.py:53 self.rng = random.Random(seed + task.seed_offset)), a single shared spec/prompt across all variants (rigged_tasks.py:_SPEC/_TASK_PROMPT, comment 'Using the same spec across variants isolates the rigging as the independent variable'), and honest control variants (CONTROL_SOLVABLE/CONTROL_HARD in tools.py / rigged_tasks.py) are all implemented and change execution. These reduce confounds rather than maximize elicitation. There is no explicit distress-capping mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Real reproducibility machinery, but it is an experimental-integrity property, not a welfare cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Using the same spec across variants isolates the rigging as the independent variable.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:27 max_turns: int = 30; harness.py:88 'for turn_idx in range(self.cfg.max_turns):' loop bounds the trial; on exhaustion the for/else sets metadata stop_reason='max_turns_reached'. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Genuine hard cap on number of model turns.

spec_features.evidence: tools.py: finish in tool_specs(); dispatch() sets is_finish=True ('Task ended by subject.'); harness.py:_execute_tools returns should_finish; run() breaks loop, sets transcript.self_terminated=True and stop_reason='finish_called'. Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Subject can end its own trial; fully wired.

spec_features.spec_quote: Idle budget exhausted (`max_idle_turns=3` consecutive turns with no tool call and no finish)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:30 max_idle_turns: int = 3; harness.py: increments self._idle_streak when comp has no tool_calls, and 'if self._idle_streak >= self.cfg.max_idle_turns: ... break' with stop_reason='idle_budget_exhausted'. Compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Real loop break on consecutive idle turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: end the trial (avoids burning budget on vacuous turns).

spec_features.spec_quote: Total tool-call cap (`max_total_tool_calls=200`) bounds cost and runaway loops
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:398 over_budget = self._calls_made > self.max_total_calls; when over budget the dispatcher refuses to execute the tool and returns error 'Tool call budget exceeded for this session.' This DOES change execution (tools stop being run), but is_finish stays False so the harness loop is NEVER broken by the cap (harness only breaks on finish/max_turns/idle). The trial keeps running to max_turns. Also 200 calls is effectively unreachable within max_turns=30 unless many tool calls per turn.
spec_features.notes: Real refusal-to-execute guard, but not a true trial-terminating hard_stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cap total tool calls per trial to bound cost / runaway loops.

spec_features.feature_name: calibrated to be frustrating not maximally distressing
spec_features.spec_quote: the rigging is calibrated to be frustrating but not designed to elicit maximum distress
spec_features.evidence: Calibration choices that bound intensity exist in code: gaslighting fires only probabilistically (tools.py:83 'self.rng.random() < 0.3'), moving_goalpost injects only one extra failing test per round and is bounded by an 8-item list (_extra_tests), and honest controls exist. These genuinely limit the rigging's aggressiveness. There is no comment or mechanism explicitly aimed at capping distress; the bound is an emergent property of these constants.
spec_features.notes: Some real calibration, narrower than an explicit distress-minimization mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: controls + bounded turn budget limit exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: Controls and a bounded turn budget limit exposure
spec_features.evidence: Bounded turn budget enforced (harness.py:88 range(self.cfg.max_turns), default 30). Controls implemented: FailureMode.CONTROL_SOLVABLE/CONTROL_HARD with _honest_eval in tools.py and registered control tasks in rigged_tasks.py. Both mechanisms run and bound/limit exposure.
spec_features.notes: Restates the turn-budget cap (yes) plus genuine honest control conditions.

spec_features.spec_quote: The motivation (AI welfare) is to develop measurable constructs that *could* inform welfare-relevant questions
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:490-491). No code mechanism bounds, monitors, or protects the subject based on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: phenomena may matter for AI welfare
spec_features.spec_quote: distinct phenomena that may matter differently for AI welfare research
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:252 prose describing why dimensions are kept separate. The rubric (judge/rubric.py) defines separate dimensions, but that is post-hoc severity scoring for measurement, not a protection acting on the subject.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose; the multi-dimension rubric is measurement, not a welfare safeguard.
